subject.title: fix(crestodian): run approval-intent classifier on the utilityModel, not flagship (#102360)

question: Should Crestodian’s host-side approval-intent classifier inherit the general utilityModel contract, including cross-provider and provider-derived small-model selection?
rationale: The patch is technically sound, but this model’s output participates in the host consent gate and utility routing can change both model quality and the provider receiving approval text; repository evidence cannot establish that product and trust-boundary intent.

options.title: Approve utility routing
options.body: Treat bounded, fail-closed approval classification as an ordinary utility task and merge this focused, documented patch.

options.title: Retain primary routing
options.body: Keep ambiguous consent interpretation on the primary model and provider because it is part of the approval security boundary.

options.title: Define dedicated routing
options.body: Pause this PR and establish a classifier-specific model and trust contract instead of inheriting the broad utility tier.

recommendation.title: Approve utility routing
recommendation.body: Treat bounded, fail-closed approval classification as an ordinary utility task and merge this focused, documented patch.

likelyOwner.reason: The classifier and its host-side consent role originate in steipete’s merged Crestodian feature work, making that the strongest available decision-owner signal.
